transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I keep going back over my work again and again. I’ll check breakers, labels, torque marks, photos—sometimes I even drive back to a site to make sure. A simple install takes way longer than it should, and people are starting to notice.
When you're doing all this re-checking, does it feel like an urge you wish you could resist but can't, or does it feel like the 'right' and necessary way for you to do the job?

It feels necessary in the moment. I keep thinking I need to go back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, photos—whatever it is—until I’m sure it’s right. But I know I’m taking way too long, and sometimes I’ll even drive back to a site to check again.

When you feel the urge to check again, is it because a specific frightening thought pops into your head—like 'something terrible will happen if I don't check'—or is it more that you just believe this is the proper, correct way things should be done?

It’s more a frightening thought. Even after I’ve checked a panel or disconnect, I start thinking maybe I missed a loose neutral or left something that could start a fire. I try to put it out of my mind, but it just keeps coming back, even on the way home.

Would you say most of your time and distress comes from the checking behaviors themselves, or from how often the frightening thoughts about something going wrong intrude on your mind throughout the day, even when you're not actively checking?

Honestly, it’s the thoughts more. Even when I know I checked the panel or disconnect, this idea keeps barging in that I missed a loose neutral or left something that could start a fire. I try to shake it off, but it follows me around—sometimes all the way home.
Do these frightening thoughts about missing something dangerous ever pop into your mind and cause distress even when you have no plan or urge to go back and check again?

Yes. It can hit me even when I’m not planning to go back. I’ll know I checked everything, but then the thought comes in that maybe I missed one loose neutral or something that could cause a fire. I try to push it away, but it keeps bothering me, sometimes all the way home.
On an average day, roughly how much total time would you say you spend actually performing the checking behaviors—like rechecking panels, retaking photos, or driving back to a site?

A few hours, probably, depending on the job. I keep going back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, and photos, and sometimes I’ll even drive back to a site. A simple install ends up taking much longer than it should.
